findings.title: withoutLeadingSlash returns slash for slash input
withFragment early return makes clearing fragment impossible
parseAuth truncates password at second colon
searchParams array values skip JSON stringify
withoutLeadingSlash returns "/" for empty input
findings.claim: withoutLeadingSlash falls back to "/" so empty string and already-stripped root become "/" instead of "". This corrupts callers like append and resolveURL that expect "" to stay empty.

findings.title: parseAuth truncates password at second colon
findings.claim: parseAuth destructures input.split(":") so a password containing ":" is truncated to the segment before the second colon and the remainder is dropped.

findings.title: searchParams array values skip JSON stringify
findings.claim: searchParams appends array elements raw while the non-array branch JSON.stringifies non-strings, so object/number/boolean values inside arrays are coerced to "[object Object]" or wrong strings instead of JSON.

findings.title: stringifyParsedURL corrupts special-protocol URLs
findings.claim: stringifyParsedURL unconditionally appends '//' after any protocol, corrupting special protocols such as data:, blob:, javascript:, and vbscript: that parseURL returns without slashes; e.g. stringifyParsedURL(parseURL('data:text/plain,hello')) produces 'data://text/plain,hello'.

findings.title: $URL href drops host for protocol-relative URLs
findings.claim: For a protocol-relative input such as '//example.com/foo', $URL stores host 'example.com' but protocol is empty, so hasProtocol is falsy and href returns only fullpath '/foo', dropping the host from href/toString.

findings.title: joinRelativeURL loses a leading ../ segment
findings.claim: A leading '..' decrements segmentsDepth, but the following normal segment increments it back, so the later prefix logic sees a non-negative depth and emits no '../'; joinRelativeURL('../a') returns 'a' and joinRelativeURL('../a','b') returns 'a/b' instead of preserving the parent reference.

findings.title: parseAuth truncates passwords containing colons
findings.claim: Destructuring input.split(':') keeps only the first two parts, so parseAuth('user:pass:word') returns password 'pass' and silently discards ':word'; the first colon is the username/password separator and later colons belong to the password.

findings.title: parseHost breaks IPv6 hosts
findings.claim: The host regex stops [^/:]* at the first colon, so parseHost('[::1]:8080') returns hostname '[' with no port instead of the IPv6 hostname and port '8080'; $URL hostname/port getters rely on this parser.

findings.title: withFragment cannot remove an existing fragment
findings.claim: The early return for !hash makes the later hash === '' removal branch unreachable, so withFragment('/foo#bar','') returns '/foo#bar' unchanged instead of removing the fragment as its documented example states.

findings.title: withBase duplicates base before a fragment
findings.claim: The base-boundary check accepts end, '/', and '?' but not '#', so withBase('/foo#bar','/foo') treats the input as not already under the base and joinURL produces '/foo/foo#bar', duplicating the base path.
